bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar makes an impressive investment pitch at AIM Congress in Dubai - Newsonair
bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | September 8, 2026 1:33 PM Bihar makes an impressive investment pitch at AIM Congress in Dubai A delegation led by Bihar Industries Minister Ms Shreyasi Singh is participating in the Annual Investment Meeting (AIM) Congress being held in Dubai from 7th to 9th September. Yesterday, the state made an impactful presentation at the event, pitching Bihar’s investment opportunities and highlighting sectors with potential for investors. Bihar stressed the strength of existing people-to-people connections, growing infrastructure and its immense human resources to attract international investments to boost industrial development, infrastructure and employment generation. The investors were informed about the seamless road connectivity, surplus power supply and extraordinary achievements in the field of enabling infrastructure as well as government policies. The Minister also took a Q&A session with the participating potential investors and answered a range of queries on the possibilities offered by the state. Addressing the gathering, Ms. Singh said that Bihar is now moving beyond its glorious past and writing a new story of development and industrial growth. She highlighted Bihar’s improved road connectivity and changing image, saying this reflects the growing confidence and self-belief in the state. She invited investors to partner with Bihar and become part of its journey towards a developed and prosperous state.

The Bureau of Energy Efficiency, under the Ministry of Power, received formal confirmation that the CCTS meets the criteria under the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism Regulations 2026. Carbon Credit Trading Scheme The Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is India’s market-based mechanism for reducing greenhouse gas emissions through tradable carbon credits. The scheme is linked to domestic carbon pricing and can be used by exporters to show that a carbon cost has already been paid in India. Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism is a border tax framework used to align the carbon cost of imported goods with the carbon cost faced by domestic producers. The UK CBAM is scheduled to begin on 1 January 2027 and applies to carbon-intensive imports. Trade Relief and Covered Goods Under the UK mechanism, importers of Indian goods can claim relief on CBAM liability for the effective carbon price already paid in India. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar plans Teacher Training University and AI ecosystem with Tech Giants
bihar_raw_news.content: News Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Copy URL The Bihar government has announced plans to establish a dedicated Teacher Training University aimed at strengthening the skills and capacity of educators across the state. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary made the announcement on Teachers’ Day, highlighting the need for continuous professional development for teachers. The proposed university will provide regular training to teachers working across different levels of education, from primary schools to higher education, engineering and polytechnic institutions. Bihar currently has more than seven lakh teachers, making large-scale capacity building a key focus of the initiative. Alongside the university, Bihar is planning to develop a modern AI ecosystem in collaboration with Microsoft, Google and Sarvam AI. Under this initiative, teachers will receive training in emerging AI technologies and tools to support more effective teaching and learning. The state has also finalised an MoU with Google specifically for AI-focused teacher training. Also Read: Odisha launches ‘AI Course for All’ to build future-ready skills The government is also exploring the establishment of a Banaras Hindu University (BHU) centre in Bihar, which could expand access to higher education opportunities for students within the state. The initiatives reflect Bihar’s broader push towards technology-enabled education, teacher development and modernisation of its education system. By combining specialised teacher training with AI adoption and collaborations with leading technology companies, the state aims to prepare educators and learners for a rapidly changing digital environment. _____________________________________________________________________ Stay informed with the latest developments shaping the future of education. bihar_raw_news.title: Patna High Court Seeks Answers From Karnataka Authorities Over Detention of Two Bihar Residents
bihar_raw_news.content: VIP MEMBER LOGIN Home Court Updates Court Updates Patna High Court Seeks Answers From Karnataka Authorities Over Detention of Two Bihar Residents By Law Trend September 8, 2026 10:34 AM Facebook WhatsApp Twitter Print Pinterest The Patna High Court has issued formal notices to Karnataka police and administrative authorities over allegations that two Bihar residents were taken into custody from Vaishali district without adhering to mandatory legal procedures. A division bench comprising Justice Rajeev Ranjan Prasad and Justice Sunil Dutta Mishra, in an order dated September 3, took strict notice of the reported lapses during the inter-state operation. The bench ordered authorities from both Bihar and Karnataka to submit comprehensive affidavits detailing the justification and circumstances surrounding the detentions, the current whereabouts of the two individuals, and any judicial processes observed during the operation. Allegations of Procedural Breaches The judicial intervention follows a writ petition moved by Shatrudhan Prasad Singh. According to the petition, Karnataka police took Alok Ambani and Aman Kumar into custody from Vaishali on August 12. The plea stated that visiting law enforcement personnel carried out the detentions without alerting local Bihar police. Furthermore, the petition alleged that officers transported the two men out of the state without securing a transit remand from a local court, circumventing statutory requirements for inter-state custody. Next Court Hearing Scheduled In response to the alleged statutory violations, the division bench mandated that both state administrations provide a full accounting of the sequence of events and clarify the legal basis under which the men were removed from Bihar. READ ALSO Supreme Court Defers Hearing in Journalist Mahesh Langa's Money-Laundering Case to April The high court has scheduled the matter for its next hearing on September 16, when the submitted affidavits will be taken on record. bihar_raw_news.title: UP, Bihar in rain zone as Delhi moves past days of heavy showers - CNBC TV18
bihar_raw_news.content: UP, Bihar in rain zone as Delhi moves past days of heavy showers Bihar, already reeling from widespread flooding and swollen rivers, could see little respite from the wet conditions. By CNBCTV18.com September 8, 2026, 5:00:56 AM IST (Published) The rain spell is likely to ease over Delhi and parts of northwest India on Tuesday, September 8, even as Bihar, West Bengal and parts of Uttar Pradesh remain under pressure from heavy rainfall. A low-pressure area over central Uttar Pradesh is driving the weather over north and east India. The India Meteorological Department has forecast fairly widespread to widespread rain over Bihar through September 9, with isolated heavy rainfall likely from September 8-10. Bihar, already reeling from widespread flooding and swollen rivers, could see little respite from the wet conditions. The state recorded 12 cm of rain at Laukahi in Madhubani in the 24 hours ending 8.30 am on Monday. The IMD has also warned of thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds in Bihar through the week. In West Bengal and Sikkim, the weather is likely to remain active, with fairly widespread to widespread rain over Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim through September 13. Gangetic West Bengal is also likely to see widespread rain through September 10, with heavy rainfall possible through September 9. East Uttar Pradesh is another area to watch on Tuesday, with isolated heavy rainfall forecast. West Uttar Pradesh could also see isolated rain, while rainfall activity over Uttarakhand is expected to be more scattered. For Delhi, the recent spell of heavy rain is set to ease significantly. The capital is forecast to see a partly cloudy sky with no warning on Tuesday, with temperatures expected to range between 25°C and 34°C. The IMD expects similar conditions over the next few days. Central India will continue to see scattered showers and thunderstorms, particularly over Madhya Pradesh and Vidarbha, while Konkan and Goa are likely to receive fairly widespread to widespread rainfall through September 13. Across the south, rainfall is expected to remain relatively subdued, with isolated to scattered showers over several states. Telangana could see gusty winds through September 9, while Kerala is likely to remain hot and humid throughout the day. Continue Reading Tags IMD forecast

bihar_raw_news.title: Tejashwi Yadav urges Centre to declare Bihar floods a national disaster
bihar_raw_news.content: Tejashwi Yadav urges Centre to declare Bihar floods a national disaster RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to declare Bihar’s floods a national disaster and provide Rs 5,000 crore in immediate assistance. He also sought enhanced rescue operations, farmer relief, an audit and a long-term flood resilience mission By IANS Published Date - 8 September 2026, 12:15 AM Patna: As severe floods continue to affect large parts of Bihar, Leader of the Opposition Tejashwi Yadav has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging the Centre to declare the situation a national disaster and provide immediate financial assistance of Rs 5,000 crore to the state. More than a dozen districts have been affected by the floods, with lakhs of people facing difficulties caused by rising river levels, damaged infrastructure and disrupted connectivity. In his letter, Yadav said the situation had affected 20 districts and caused extensive damage to life, property and public infrastructure. He said flood-affected people were struggling to access basic necessities, including food, clean drinking water, medicines, electricity, cattle fodder and safe transportation. Yadav criticised the relief and rescue measures being undertaken by the Bihar government and the NDA-led Centre, describing the assistance as inadequate considering the scale of the crisis. He also accused the Bihar government and NDA leaders from the state of failing to secure adequate central assistance and a national-disaster declaration. The RJD leader argued that Bihar’s recurring floods are not solely a natural disaster but also reflect years of inadequate disaster preparedness, mitigation and adaptation. He pointed out that despite floods occurring almost every year, sufficient measures for a permanent solution have not been implemented. Yadav also raised questions over the state government’s financial preparedness for the crisis. He alleged that Bihar’s Contingency Fund and other financial resources had been diverted towards routine government expenditure, leaving insufficient funds for flood relief. The RJD leader called for an independent review or CAG audit of the state’s financial and disaster-management preparedness and the utilisation of the State Contingency Fund. In his letter, Yadav urged the Prime Minister and the Central Government to take immediate measures, including declare the devastating floods in Bihar a national disaster, provide Rs 5,000 crore in immediate financial assistance along with a special flood-relief package, deploy additional boats and other resources to flood-hit areas where road connectivity has been disrupted, deploy the Army and Air Force wherever necessary for rescue and relief operations and ensure assistance through helicopters, ensure adequate supplies of food, drinking water, medicines, animal fodder and temporary shelters, provide special financial assistance to farmers, labourers, livestock owners and affected families, and conduct an independent review or CAG audit of the state’s disaster-management preparedness and the utilisation and transactions of the State Contingency Fund. Yadav also called for a comprehensive, long-term Flood Resilience Mission to address Bihar’s recurring flood crisis. According to him, the mission should focus on river and embankment management, drainage systems, rejuvenation of water bodies, modern flood forecasting and improved water-management policies. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Gujarat and Maharashtra today. In Gujarat, Prime Minister will lay the foundation stones, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over 35 thousand crore rupees from Vadodara. Mr Modi will also dedicate to the nation three important sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC), marking completion of the project. Talking to media persons at Ahmedabad airport, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that this mega-project has now been fully completed and will be formally dedicated to the nation by the Prime Minister. A major highlight of the PM’s visit will be the dedication of three key sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor spanning 326 route kilometres. Built at a cost exceeding ₹20,700 crore, this marks the full completion and operationalisation of the Freight Corridor network. The Prime Minister will also flag off freight train services from New Sanand, New Makarpura, New Umbergaon, and New JNPT, along with a new passenger train service between Tanda Road and Vadodara, connecting remote tribal regions of Alirajpur to the national rail grid. In addition, Mr Modi will also lay the foundation stone for three railway expansion projects worth over ₹9,700 crore and three National Highway projects costing around ₹1,780 crore to ease congestion and boost connectivity across Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh. He will also launch various civic and infrastructure projects of Gujarat Government worth ₹2,600 crore, including a 110 Megawatt floating solar plant at Kadana Dam and PMAY housing units. Later, the PM will also visit Navsari to inaugurate the BJP’s new AI-enabled, high-tech office in Navsari.” In Maharashtra, the Prime Minister will inaugurate the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 in Mumbai and address the gathering. The theme of GFF 2026 is, “Potential to Impact: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum – Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance.” The GFF 2026 seeks to build on India’s leadership in digital payments and financial inclusion and move from potential to impact. The discussions will focus on how AI, programmable finance, quantum technologies and other critical and emerging technologies can create trusted, inclusive and measurable outcomes for citizens, enterprises and economies globally. Since 2020, Global Fintech Fest has emerged as a leadership platform, bringing together policymakers, regulators, central banks, financial institutions, fintechs, technology companies, investors, academia and other global stakeholders to discuss and shape the future of finance. The seventh edition will run till 11th September 2026 in Mumbai.

national_raw_news.title: 43 mins ago | National 331 DAC clears acquisition proposals worth over Rs 1.10 lakh cr for Forces
national_raw_news.content: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) today cleared capital acquisition proposals worth over 1.10 lakh crore rupees for the defence forces. The approval was granted during a meeting of the Council held under the Chairmanship of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. The proposals include, procurement of Chemical Biological Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Recce Vehicles, High Mobility Vehicles (HMV), Self-Propelled Mechanical Mine Layers (MML), Advanced Light Helicopters (ALHs), Trawl Tanks and Sarvatra Bridge System for the Indian Army. For the Indian Navy, Acceptance of Necessity was accorded for the procurement of Arudhra Radars, Design and Development and subsequent procurement of Marine Gas Turbines (MGT). Arudhra Radar will replace the existing Air Route Surveillance Radars at various Naval Air Stations and MGT, a warship propulsion system, will reduce dependency on foreign vendors. Meanwhile, for the Indian Air Force, approval was granted to various proposals to enhance the war-fighting capability of fighters, transports and helicopters. Approval was also accorded for procuring Ground-Based Multi-Purpose Jammer (GBMPJ) and installing Defence Forces Secure Access Card (DEFSAC) System. Defence Ministry said that 98 percent of total procurements will be made from the Indian Industry. The CBRN Recce Vehicles will be capable of detecting, identifying, monitoring and marking of areas contaminated with CBRN agents. The HMVs will enhance operational capabilities, logistic support and mobility in challenging terrains. The MMLs will achieve the desired operational capability in terms of fast and responsive minelaying in difficult terrains. The ALHs will execute complex missions across all terrains and operational situations for the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force. The Trawl Tanks and Bridge System will be utilised to provide composite crossings to fighting formations during operations in varied terrains. The GBMPJ will provide effective jamming against radars of adversaries and DEFSAC will replace existing paper based Identity Card, Passes, Permits with an interoperable Radio Frequency Identification-based smart cards system.

national_raw_news.title: 44 mins ago | National 111 India joins 24 countries in global initiative on 6G technology
national_raw_news.content: India has joined the United States and 24 other countries in an international initiative aimed at shaping the development of next-generation 6G networks. In a social media post, the US Department of Commerce said, India had joined the US and 24 other countries in an effort to ensure that next-generation networks reflect shared security interests, strengthen competitiveness and drive innovation. The announcement came after Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada met US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on the sidelines of the G20 Innovation Ministerial. The two leaders discussed the future of 6G technology and the importance of international cooperation in developing next-generation telecommunications networks. During the meeting, India and the US discussed strengthening cooperation in semiconductors, AI and data centres. MoS Prasada encouraged the possibility of more US investments in ISM 2.0, proposed strengthening AI technology partnership and shared a mechanism for safeguards for AI. Jitin Prasada led the Indian delegation at the G20 Innovation Minister’s meeting held on September 1 and September 2 in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, United States, hosted by the US Department of Commerce and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP). The meeting concluded with the G20 Innovation Ministerial Statement, highlighting the potential of emerging technologies to drive prosperity, productivity and opportunity. India reaffirmed its commitment to building strategic partnerships in AI, semiconductors, DPI, robotics and other emerging technologies into greater opportunities for innovation, economic growth and an improved quality of life for its citizens.

national_raw_news.title: Arunachal media delegation explores Gujarat's development journey, heritage and infrastructure
national_raw_news.content: Echo Of Arunachal Newsflash State News Arunachal media delegation explores Gujarat’s development journey, heritage and infrastructure Ahmedabad, Sep 7: A nine-member media delegation from Arunachal Pradesh began its seven-day press tour of Gujarat on Monday, visiting key institutions and projects showcasing the State’s development in governance, urban planning, heritage and transport infrastructure. The tour commenced at the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Ahmedabad, where the delegation was welcomed by Additional Director General Siddhartha Bodke. Interacting with the visiting journalists, Bodke briefed them on PIB’s role in disseminating information on government policies, programmes and initiatives and encouraged the media team to make the most of the field visits and expert interactions lined up during the tour. The delegation next visited Kochrab Ashram, Mahatma Gandhi's first ashram established after returning from South Africa in 1915, where the journalists interacted with Dr Prasana Gandhi, who briefed them on the historical and cultural significance of the Ashram and its association with the Father of the Nation, his philosophy and India’s freedom movement. The journalists also undertook a cruise on the Sabarmati River, observing the riverfront development and the surrounding urban landscape. The visit provided an opportunity to understand Ahmedabad’s riverfront transformation and its integration with the city’s urban development. At Centre for Environmental Planning and Technology (CEPT) University, the delegation interacted with President Barjor Mehta and senior faculty members on architecture, urban planning, education and research. The interaction also covered the institution’s contribution to shaping urban environments through education and research. The first day concluded with a visit to the Sabarmati Multimodal Transport Hub, where the delegation was briefed on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) project. The interaction covered the scale and technical complexity of India’s first high-speed rail corridor, including engineering, planning, inter-agency coordination and on-ground execution. During the visit, Joint Director, PIB Itanagar, Utsav Parmar, also called on Principal Chief Project Manager Rajesh Agarwal. The seven-day press tour will take the Arunachal media delegation to several key sites and institutions across Gujarat, covering infrastructure, industry, technology, education, heritage and culture. The tour is aimed at providing the journalists with direct field exposure to major development initiatives and projects shaping Gujarat, enabling them to gain a broader understanding of the State’s development experience and its relevance to the diverse development landscape of the country. The delegation raised various issues relating to the banking sector including review of ex-gratia, medical facility for retired employees, revisiting the present structure of Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme applicable for the employees of PSBs, and other concerns related to employees. The tour has been organised by the Press Information Bureau, Kochi, with the stated objective of giving Kerala based journalists direct exposure to ground realities in Jammu and Kashmir rather than relying solely on secondhand reporting or official briefings from Delhi. Such cross regional press tours have increasingly become a tool used by the government to encourage journalists from other parts of the country to engage directly with regions like Kashmir, whose coverage in the national media has historically been shaped heavily by security and conflict narratives. On the opening day of the tour, the delegation visited the Press Information Bureau office in Srinagar, where Director Quazi Salman welcomed the visiting journalists and walked them through the media and communication landscape of Kashmir. Salman’s briefing is understood to have covered the functioning of PIB in the region, giving the delegation an institutional grounding before they proceed to visit specific project sites and locations over the remainder of the week. Later on the first day, the delegation travelled to Gulmarg, the well known hill station in Baramulla district, where members experienced the region’s natural landscape and scenic beauty firsthand. The choice of Gulmarg as an early stop reflects both its standing as one of Kashmir’s most recognisable destinations and its symbolic value in showcasing the valley’s tourism appeal to visiting journalists who may go on to write about the region for audiences back home in Kerala. Over the remaining days of the tour, the delegation is expected to visit a range of developmental projects and significant locations across the Union Territory, with organisers framing the itinerary around familiarising participants with the pace of infrastructural and developmental transformation underway in Jammu and Kashmir. The tour is also expected to include structured interactions with local stakeholders, giving journalists an opportunity to engage directly with officials and residents rather than observe projects from a distance.
